question.prompt: Set \(A\) has \(20\) elements, and set \(B\) has \(15\) elements. What is the smallest possible number of elements in \(A \cup B,\) the union of \(A\) and \(B?\)

solutions.explanation:
The union contains every element belonging to either set, counting shared elements only once. Since it contains all \(20\) elements of \(A\), it cannot have fewer than \(20\) elements.

This lower bound is attainable: choose all \(15\) elements of \(B\) from \(A\). Then \(B\subseteq A\), so \(B\) contributes no new elements and \(A\cup B=A\).

Therefore the smallest possible number is \(20\), choice C.
solutions.title: Place the smaller set inside the larger
